anlamlar.tr: (bir şey hakkında) ne düşünmek, nasıl yorumlamak
anlamlar.en: to have an opinion about someone or something
ornekler: What do you make of the new teacher?
I don't know what to make of his message.

anlamlar.en: to change something into something else
ornekler: They made the old barn into a house.
The book was made into a film.

anlamlar.en: to plan something in detail
ornekler: She has mapped out her whole career.
Let's map out the next six months.

anlamlar.en: to reduce the price of something
ornekler: All winter coats have been marked down.
The shoes were marked down by 30%.

anlamlar.en: to give a lower grade
ornekler: You'll be marked down for poor spelling.
The teacher marked me down for being late.

anlamlar.en: to be good enough
ornekler: The new player didn't measure up.
Does the hotel measure up to its reviews?

anlamlar.en: to meet someone, usually by arrangement
ornekler: Let's meet up for coffee next week.
We met up with some friends in town.

anlamlar.en: to think carefully about something for a long time
ornekler: I need some time to mull it over.
She mulled over the job offer for a week.

anlamlar.en: to reach a final and certain decision about something
ornekler: We still need to nail down the date.
They finally nailed down the deal.

anlamlar.en: to put your things into bags or boxes, often before leaving
ornekler: We packed up and left the hotel.
Pack up your books – the lesson is over.

anlamlar.en: to stop working
ornekler: My old laptop finally packed up.
The engine packed up on the way home.

anlamlar.en: to develop or happen in a particular way
ornekler: Let's see how things pan out.
The plan didn't pan out as we hoped.

anlamlar.en: to pretend that something or someone is something else
ornekler: He tried to pass off the painting as an original.
She passed herself off as a doctor.

anlamlar.en: to not choose someone for a job or promotion
ornekler: She was passed over for promotion again.
He felt he had been passed over.

anlamlar.en: to spend or pay a large amount of money
ornekler: The insurance company paid out millions after the storm.
We paid out a lot for the wedding.

anlamlar.en: to eat only a small amount of food, slowly and without interest
ornekler: She just picked at her dinner.
He picked at his salad and said nothing.

anlamlar.en: to stop talking or be quieter
ornekler: Pipe down, kids – I'm on the phone!
Could you pipe down a bit?

anlamlar.en: to start to work with other people to get something done
ornekler: Everyone pitched in to clean up after the party.
If we all pitch in, we'll finish quickly.

anlamlar.en: to pretend to agree with someone or do what they want
ornekler: I knew it was a joke, but I played along.
Just play along and don't say anything.

anlamlar.en: to behave in a silly way, or to try different things to see what works
ornekler: Stop playing around and get dressed!
I played around with the settings until it worked.

anlamlar.en: to use someone's feelings or weaknesses to get what you want
ornekler: The ads play on people's fears.
He played on her kindness.

anlamlar.en: to happen or develop in a particular way
ornekler: Let's see how the situation plays out.
The drama played out in front of the cameras.

anlamlar.en: to make something seem more important than it is
ornekler: The newspapers played up the story.
He played up his experience in the interview.

anlamlar.en: to cause problems or behave badly
ornekler: My knee is playing up again.
The kids were playing up all day.

anlamlar.en: to show that something is likely to be true
ornekler: All the evidence points to him.
Studies point to a link between sleep and memory.

anlamlar.en: to finish something quickly, especially food
ornekler: He polished off the whole pizza.
I polished off my homework in an hour.

anlamlar.en: to continue doing something in a determined way
ornekler: Despite the rain, we pressed on.
We must press on with the project.

anlamlar.en: to separate something into pieces
ornekler: The dog pulled the pillow apart.
Pull the bread apart with your hands.

anlamlar.en: to criticize something severely
ornekler: The critics pulled her new book apart.
He pulled my essay apart.

anlamlar.en: to start moving away (a vehicle)
ornekler: The bus pulled away just as I arrived.
She watched the train pull away.

anlamlar.en: to move away from someone who is holding you
ornekler: She pulled away when he tried to hug her.
He pulled away from the crowd.

anlamlar.en: to move back or decide not to do something
ornekler: The troops pulled back from the border.
The company pulled back from the deal.

anlamlar.en: to work together to achieve something
ornekler: If we all pull together, we can do it.
The community pulled together after the flood.

anlamlar.en: to control your feelings and start behaving calmly
ornekler: Pull yourself together and stop crying.
She pulled herself together and went back inside.

anlamlar.en: to continue with a plan in a determined way
ornekler: The government is pushing ahead with the reforms.
They pushed ahead despite the protests.

anlamlar.en: to change the time of an event to a later time
ornekler: The meeting has been pushed back to Friday.
The launch was pushed back a month.

anlamlar.en: to oppose a plan or idea
ornekler: Students pushed back against the new rules.
The team pushed back on the decision.

anlamlar.tr: (bir şey için) ısrar etmek, baskı yapmak
anlamlar.en: to try hard to achieve something or make it happen
ornekler: Parents are pushing for longer school vacations.
We're pushing for better pay.

anlamlar.en: to get a law or plan accepted despite opposition
ornekler: The government pushed through the new law.
They pushed the changes through quickly.

anlamlar.en: to think that something is caused by something else
ornekler: I put his rudeness down to stress.
She put her success down to hard work.

anlamlar.en: to encourage someone to do something wrong or silly
ornekler: Who put you up to this?
His friends put him up to the prank.

anlamlar.en: to read a lot about a subject in order to learn about it
ornekler: I read up on the company before the interview.
You should read up on the history of the city.

anlamlar.en: to make a new product or service available
ornekler: The company will roll out the new app next month.
The vaccine was rolled out across the country.

anlamlar.en: to find and get rid of something bad
ornekler: We must root out corruption.
The new boss rooted out lazy workers.

anlamlar.en: to keep talking about someone's mistake to make them feel bad
ornekler: I know I was wrong – there's no need to rub it in.
He kept rubbing it in that he'd won.

anlamlar.en: to remove writing with an eraser
ornekler: Rub out the wrong answer and try again.
She rubbed out the drawing.

anlamlar.en: to tell someone about an idea to see what they think
ornekler: Can I run an idea by you?
Run it by your manager first.

anlamlar.en: to try to be elected to a position
ornekler: She's running for mayor.
He ran for president twice.

anlamlar.en: to leave a place or person suddenly
ornekler: The boys ran off when they saw the police.
He ran off with all the money.

anlamlar.en: to quickly print copies of something
ornekler: Can you run off ten copies of this?
I ran off a few copies of the report.

anlamlar.en: to make a debt or bill larger by spending money
ornekler: He ran up a huge phone bill.
They ran up debts of over $10,000.

anlamlar.en: to have to deal with an unexpected difficulty
ornekler: The plan ran up against strong opposition.
We ran up against a few problems.

anlamlar.en: to make something smaller in size or amount
ornekler: The company has scaled back its plans.
We had to scale back the party.

anlamlar.en: to manage to live with very little money
ornekler: They scraped by on one small salary.
Many students just scrape by.

anlamlar.en: to deal with something or arrange for something to be done
ornekler: I'll see about getting the window fixed.
We'll see about that later.

anlamlar.en: to look for someone or something, especially for a long time
ornekler: She sought out the best doctors.
Tourists seek out quiet beaches.

anlamlar.en: to sell something, often cheaply, because you need money or do not need it
ornekler: The company sold off its old factories.
They're selling off last year's stock.

anlamlar.en: to ask someone to come to you
ornekler: Send for a doctor!
The principal sent for his parents.

anlamlar.en: to send something to an organization
ornekler: Viewers sent in their photos.
Please send in your application by Friday.

anlamlar.en: to send soldiers or police to deal with a situation
ornekler: The army was sent in to help after the earthquake.
They sent in the police.

anlamlar.en: to decide on something after considering many options
ornekler: We finally settled on a name for the baby.
They settled on a small hotel by the sea.

anlamlar.en: to get rid of an illness or something unpleasant
ornekler: I can't shake off this cold.
She couldn't shake off the feeling that something was wrong.

anlamlar.en: to escape from someone who is following you
ornekler: He shook off the reporters.
The thief managed to shake off the police.

anlamlar.en: to make big changes to an organization or system
ornekler: The new manager wants to shake up the company.
The election shook up the government.

anlamlar.en: to upset or shock someone
ornekler: The accident really shook him up.
She was badly shaken up by the news.

anlamlar.en: to increase very quickly
ornekler: Prices have shot up this year.
The number of students shot up.

anlamlar.en: to grow quickly in height
ornekler: Your son has really shot up!
She shot up over the summer.

anlamlar.en: to treat something as unimportant
ornekler: He shrugged off the criticism.
She shrugged off her injury and kept playing.

anlamlar.en: to prevent someone or something from entering, or to stop yourself thinking about something
ornekler: Close the curtains to shut out the light.
She tries to shut out painful memories.

anlamlar.en: to choose one person or thing from a group for special attention
ornekler: The teacher singled her out for praise.
Why single me out? Everyone was talking.

anlamlar.en: to watch a class or meeting without taking part
ornekler: Can I sit in on your lesson?
A manager sat in on the interview.

anlamlar.en: to not take part in an activity
ornekler: I'll sit out this dance.
He had to sit out the game with an injury.

anlamlar.tr: (sıkıcı bir şeyi) sonuna kadar oturup izlemek
anlamlar.en: to stay until the end of something boring or long
ornekler: We had to sit through a three-hour meeting.
I can't sit through that film again.

anlamlar.en: to look at someone or something carefully to form an opinion
ornekler: She sized up the situation quickly.
The two players sized each other up.

anlamlar.en: to wait until the next day before deciding something
ornekler: I'll sleep on it and tell you tomorrow.
Why don't you sleep on it?

anlamlar.en: to leave quietly, or to gradually disappear
ornekler: He slipped away before the end of the party.
Their chance of winning was slipping away.

anlamlar.en: to buy or get something quickly because it is cheap or popular
ornekler: The tickets were snapped up in minutes.
Shoppers snapped up the bargains.

anlamlar.en: to talk to someone to discover what they think about something
ornekler: I'll sound out the boss about the idea.
We sounded out a few customers.

anlamlar.en: to state your opinion publicly, especially to oppose something
ornekler: She spoke out against the plan.
More people should speak out about bullying.

anlamlar.en: to get rid of something bad
ornekler: The school is trying to stamp out bullying.
We must stamp out racism.

anlamlar.en: to leave an important job or position
ornekler: The chairman stood down after ten years.
She stood down as party leader.

anlamlar.en: to do someone's job for a short time
ornekler: Can you stand in for me tomorrow?
The assistant stood in for the manager.

anlamlar.en: to defend yourself against a more powerful person
ornekler: You must stand up to bullies.
She stood up to her boss.

anlamlar.en: to not be damaged by something
ornekler: These boots stand up to heavy use.
Will the theory stand up to examination?

anlamlar.en: to begin your life or career in a particular way
ornekler: She started out as a waitress.
We started out with only two employees.

anlamlar.en: to start a business, or to start working (a machine)
ornekler: He started up his own company.
The car won't start up.

anlamlar.en: to not go somewhere or near someone
ornekler: Stay away from my sister!
Many fans stayed away because of the rain.

anlamlar.en: to continue to stay somewhere after others have left or after the expected time
ornekler: She stayed on at school for another year.
He stayed on as a coach.

anlamlar.en: to not come home at night or until late
ornekler: Don't stay out too late.
He stayed out all night.

anlamlar.en: to move to one side, or to leave a job so someone else can do it
ornekler: Please step aside and let them pass.
The director stepped aside for a younger leader.

anlamlar.en: to stop and think about something from a distance
ornekler: Let's step back and look at the whole picture.
Sometimes you need to step back from your work.

anlamlar.en: to offer to help
ornekler: Several people stepped forward to help.
Nobody stepped forward with information.

anlamlar.en: to stay somewhere for a period of time
ornekler: Stick around after class – I want to talk to you.
I didn't stick around for the end of the party.

anlamlar.en: to support each other
ornekler: Friends should stick together.
The team stuck together through hard times.

anlamlar.tr: (bir şeye, birine) bağlı kalmak, devam etmek
anlamlar.en: to continue doing or using something
ornekler: I'll stick with my old phone.
If you stick with it, you'll improve.

anlamlar.en: to cause trouble or strong feelings
ornekler: He's always trying to stir up trouble.
The film stirred up old memories.

anlamlar.en: to visit somewhere for a short time
ornekler: I'll stop by your house later.
Stop by the office when you have time.

anlamlar.en: to stop somewhere for a short time during a journey
ornekler: We stopped off in Paris for two days.
Let's stop off at the shop on the way home.

anlamlar.en: to stay somewhere for a short time during a long journey
ornekler: We stopped over in Dubai on the way to Australia.
The flight stops over in Istanbul.

anlamlar.en: to deal with a problem or confusing situation
ornekler: We need to straighten out this mess.
I'll straighten things out with the bank.

anlamlar.en: to start a conversation or relationship with someone
ornekler: He struck up a conversation with the woman next to him.
They struck up a friendship on vacation.

anlamlar.en: to treat someone badly because you are angry or upset about something else
ornekler: Don't take it out on me!
He takes his stress out on his family.

anlamlar.en: to start to like someone or something
ornekler: The kids took to their new teacher immediately.
She took to the job very quickly.

anlamlar.en: to start doing something as a habit
ornekler: He's taken to going for long walks.
She took to reading in bed.

anlamlar.en: to answer someone rudely
ornekler: Don't talk back to your mother!
He was sent out for talking back.

anlamlar.en: to talk to someone as if they were less intelligent than you
ornekler: I hate it when people talk down to me.
Don't talk down to the students.

anlamlar.en: to discuss something in detail so that someone understands it
ornekler: Let me talk you through the process.
We talked through the problem together.

anlamlar.en: to tell someone in authority about something bad that someone has done
ornekler: If you do that again, I'll tell on you.
She told on her brother.

anlamlar.en: to have a bad effect on someone
ornekler: The stress is beginning to tell on him.
Years of hard work told on her health.

anlamlar.en: to think about what might happen in the future and plan for it
ornekler: It's important to think ahead when you travel.
Good players always think ahead.

anlamlar.en: to think about something that happened in the past
ornekler: Think back to your first day at school.
When I think back, I was very lucky.

anlamlar.en: to include something extra with something you are selling, without charging more
ornekler: If you buy the TV, we'll throw in the cable for free.
They threw in a free dessert.

anlamlar.en: to add a remark to a conversation
ornekler: She threw in a few jokes during her talk.
He threw in a comment about the weather.

anlamlar.en: to warn someone secretly about something that will happen
ornekler: Someone tipped off the police.
The journalist was tipped off about the scandal.

anlamlar.en: to make something less strong or offensive
ornekler: You should tone down your language.
The ad was toned down after complaints.

anlamlar.en: to land on the ground (a plane)
ornekler: The plane touched down at 6 a.m.
We touched down in Rome on time.

anlamlar.en: to mention a subject briefly
ornekler: The lecture touched on several important issues.
I'd like to touch on one more point.

anlamlar.en: to make small changes to improve something
ornekler: She touched up her make-up before the meeting.
The photo had been touched up.

anlamlar.en: to give something old as part of the payment for something new
ornekler: I traded in my old car for a new one.
You can trade in your old phone.

anlamlar.en: to make someone fall, or to make someone make a mistake
ornekler: He tripped up on the stairs.
The last question tripped up many students.

anlamlar.en: to watch or listen to a broadcast
ornekler: Millions tuned in to watch the final.
Tune in next week for the next episode.

anlamlar.en: to start to dislike or oppose someone you liked before
ornekler: His friends turned against him.
Public opinion turned against the war.

anlamlar.en: to go to someone or something for help or advice
ornekler: She has no one to turn to.
He turned to his parents for help.

anlamlar.en: to start doing or using something
ornekler: After the war, he turned to writing.
Let's turn to the next topic.

anlamlar.en: to not go to bed until someone comes home
ornekler: Don't wait up for me – I'll be late.
My mom always waits up for me.

anlamlar.en: to leave a difficult situation instead of dealing with it
ornekler: You can't just walk away from your problems.
He walked away from the deal.

anlamlar.en: to come out of an accident without serious injury
ornekler: She walked away from the crash without a scratch.
Both drivers walked away unhurt.

anlamlar.en: to win a prize easily, or to take something that is not yours
ornekler: She walked off with first prize.
Someone walked off with my umbrella.

anlamlar.en: to make something smaller by using it, or to make someone tired and weak
ornekler: The steps were worn down by years of use.
The long fight wore him down.

anlamlar.en: to remove people or things that are not wanted
ornekler: The test is designed to weed out weak candidates.
We need to weed out the mistakes.

anlamlar.en: to spend time in a relaxed way
ornekler: We whiled away the afternoon by the pool.
He whiled away the hours reading.

anlamlar.en: to get back something that you had lost
ornekler: The party is trying to win back voters.
He wanted to win back her trust.

anlamlar.en: to persuade someone to support you or agree with you
ornekler: She won over the audience with her speech.
It took time to win him over.

anlamlar.en: to finally be in a particular place or situation
ornekler: We wound up in a little bar by the sea.
If you keep driving like that, you'll wind up in hospital.

anlamlar.en: to end something
ornekler: Let's wind up the meeting.
The project will wind up in June.

anlamlar.en: to get rid of something by doing physical activity
ornekler: I went for a run to work off my anger.
She's trying to work off the extra weight.

anlamlar.tr: (bir sorunu) adım adım çözmek, üstesinden gelmek
anlamlar.en: to deal with a problem or emotion until it is solved
ornekler: We need to work through these issues together.
It takes time to work through grief.

anlamlar.en: to develop a feeling or quality, especially by effort
ornekler: I worked up the courage to ask her out.
A long walk works up an appetite.

anlamlar.en: to make someone excited or upset
ornekler: Don't get so worked up about it!
He worked himself up into a state.

anlamlar.en: to direct all your attention to one thing
ornekler: The police zeroed in on the main suspect.
Let's zero in on the most important problem.

anlamlar.en: to stop paying attention and not notice what is happening around you
ornekler: I zoned out during the lecture.
Sorry, I zoned out – what did you say?
